children: Maturing crops in the Plains and Midwest are seeing depleting soil moisture this week, with high temperatures crossing 100°F and pushing crops towards being harvest-ready faster. The NOAA's Climate Prediction Center is forecasting above-average temperatures across the U.S. Corn Belt over the next 6-10 days, only slightly moderating through the next 14 days. The grain market is closely watching to see how much hot weather has impacted the health of crops, with last month's Pro Farmer Midwest Crop Tour revealing that heat stress hurt crops and reporting lower output forecasts versus the same time the prior year. Grains are mixed, with most-active corn up 0.3%, soybeans down 0.2%, and wheat off 0.2%. (kirk.maltais@wsj.com)
